This is the README file for FracVAL_v1 containing the following information:
1. About FracVAL
2. CC-FracVAL, modules and input parameters
3. Installation and execution
4. Understanding the output files

FracVAL: FracVAL: An Improved Tunable Algorithm of Cluster-Cluster Aggregation for Generation of Fractal Structures Formed by Polydisperse Primary Particles
Authors: J. Morán (jose.moranc@alumnos.usm.cl), A. Fuentes, F. Liu & J.Yon

1. About FracVAL
FracVAL consists is an algorithm designed for the numerical generation of fractal-like aggregates 
with specific morphology. For the version FracVAL_v1 aggregates consist of point-touching, spherical 
polydisperse primary particles.

* FracVAL: A number of sub-clusters are generated by using a particle-cluster approach, then a hierarchical 
cluster-cluster aggregation takes place.

2. FracVAL
2.1. Architecture of the algorithm
* FracVAL_CCA: This is the main module of CC-FracVAL, its goal is to do an iterative process until generating the 
  required number of aggregates defined by the user.
* Ctes: This module contain all the parameters used by the algorithm.
* CCA: This is the core module of PC-FracVAL. Its aim is the generation of one aggregate at the time by following 
  an iterative process as described in the manuscript.
* PCA_Subclusters_module: This is the main module of particle-cluster subroutine, its goal is to 
  do an iterative process until generating the required number of initial sub-clusters defined by the user.
* PCA_cca: This is the core module of the particle-cluster subroutine. Its aim is the generation of one 
  sub-cluster at the time by following an iterative process as described in the User_Manual.
* Random_PP: Generate a specific quantity of numbers by using the module called "random".
* random: Contain the a pseudo-random number generator where the user can select a specific probability density function.
* RAND_SAMPLE: A module that contain a function used for the random sampling of one value from a vector or matrix.

2.2. INPUT Parameters
The parameters related with aggregates morphology are described as follows,
* N: The number of monomers in an aggregate. 
* Df: The fractal dimension. 
* kf: The fractal prefactor.
Regarding primary particle polydispersity,
* rp_g: Geometric primary particle mean.
* rp_gstd: Geometric primary particle standard deviation.
Other parameters,
* Nsubcl_perc: Number of monomers of each sub-cluster (as a percentage of N). It is used by the module "PCA_cca".
* Quantity_aggregates: Defines the number of aggregates to be generated by running once the module "FracVAL_PCA".
* tol_ov: A tolerance value used by the module "PCA" to ensure that primary particles will be in one point-contact.
  
3. Installation and execution
3.1. Installation
FracVAL was developed in the language FORTRAN 90, i.e. a Fortran compiler is required. 
We recommend the use of gfortran (free available from: https://gcc.gnu.org/wiki/GFortranBinaries).
3.2. Execution
For both Windows and Linux the programs can be executed by using an IDE such as Eclipse or Netbeans,
or also by using the respective terminal. Note that always gfortran compiler should be installed in
the computer (see section 4.1). Here we will describe the execution by using the terminals.
3.2.1. Execution in Windows:
	- Open the cmd Terminal
	- Search the containing folder: C:\...\FracVAL_v1\PROGRAM_source_codes\Windows\FRAC_VAL_CCA
	- Write the following commands: gfortran Frac_VAL_CCA.f90 Ctes.f90 CCA_module.f90 PCA_cca.f90 PCA_Subclusters_module.f90 RAND_SAMPLE.f90 random.f90 a_Random_PP.f90 Save_results_CC.f90 -o FRACVAL_CCA_executable.exe
	  IMPORTANT: If a ".mod" file is not generated, then TRY AGAIN.
	- Once all the required ".mod" have been generated. Write the following commands: FRACVAL_CCA_executable.exe
3.2.2. Execution in Linux:
	- Open the Ubuntu's Terminal
	- Search the containing folder: C:/.../FracVAL_v1/PROGRAM_source_codes/Linux/FRAC_VAL_CCA
	- Write the following commands: gfortran Frac_VAL_CCA.f90 Ctes.f90 CCA_module.f90 PCA_cca.f90 PCA_Subclusters_module.f90 RAND_SAMPLE.f90 random.f90 a_Random_PP.f90 Save_results_CC.f90 -o FRACVAL_CCA_executable
	- Write the following commands: ./FRACVAL_CCA_executable
	
4. Understanding the output files
The results are created as ".DAT" files and saved in the "RESULTS" folder. 

Each row corresponds to each monomer. 
The first 3 columns correspond to the X,Y,Z coordinates respectively. 
The column 4 corresponds to the radius of each monomer.
